findings.title: Dependency validation and revocation are separated from insertion by unlocked transactions
findings.evidence: add_record commits dependency checks at 468, appends ledger at 471, then inserts edges in a new transaction at 495-568. revoke_record snapshots closure and commits at 639 before its updates at 663-680. query_active_memories filters only record status, not upstream status (848-859).
findings.trigger: An add validates ACTIVE parent; concurrent revoke snapshots existing children and revokes parent; add then inserts its child and edges. Alternatively a child is added after the revocation closure snapshot.
findings.impact: The new child remains ACTIVE and retrievable despite its revoked dependency, outside the revocation closure. These are synchronous methods but independent engines/threads/processes use separate SQLite connections.

findings.title: Ledger acknowledgement precedes durable memory-state mutation without recovery
findings.evidence: revoke_record commits MEMORY_RECORD_REVOKED through append_event before opening the mutation transaction at 663. Ledger append commits independently (cortex_persist_ledger.py:257-271); engine constructor only initializes schema, without projection replay. add_record and retract_attribution use the same pattern.
findings.trigger: Process stops or the second database transaction fails after ledger append succeeds and before memory updates commit.
findings.impact: A durable revocation receipt can coexist with an ACTIVE readable record after reopening; committed additions can lack their memory projection. No runtime execution was performed.

findings.title: Revocation silently truncates dependency closure after 1024 levels
findings.evidence: Recursive closure uses c.depth < 1024; add_record accepts arbitrarily deep acyclic dependency chains. The returned total_invalidated does not signal truncation. Retraction has the same bound at 1062-1075.
findings.trigger: Create an acyclic dependency chain deeper than 1024 and revoke its root.
findings.impact: Nodes beyond the bound remain ACTIVE and retain their blobs; advertised transitive revocation is incomplete.

findings.title: Policy epoch rolls back on engine restart
findings.evidence: __init__ unconditionally initializes _host_epoch to 1; advance_policy_epoch (333-340) updates only this instance field. add_record signs and records using that field, while get_record accepts stored epoch without comparing a persistent host minimum.
findings.trigger: Advance epoch above 1, reopen MemoryGovernanceEngine on the same database, register principal key, then create a record.
findings.impact: New records are issued under epoch 1 despite previously advancing the authoritative epoch, contradicting monotonic policy governance.

findings.title: Python-only counter loop is described as Rust FFI and SPMC validation
findings.evidence: Header claims lock-free Python/Rust coupling; FFIWriter constructs a local ctypes structure (42), never loads a Rust library or starts a reader; run_stress_test only publishes sequentially and asserts counter parity (76-97). _pack_=1 is also not a cache-line alignment guarantee.
findings.trigger: Use this demo success as evidence for the declared cross-language seqlock/SPMC property.
findings.impact: The example cannot establish ABI coupling, concurrent reader coherence or lock-free ordering. No production caller was located by targeted search; finding is confined to example/evidence claims.

findings.title: Example formal gate approves a truthy field without checking a proof
findings.evidence: audit_ast_closure only checks truthiness of formal_proof and claim/premise overlap, then hashes repr and returns PENDING_ATTESTATION at 77-78. The surrounding text presents it as deterministic formal closure validation.
findings.trigger: Supply a nonempty arbitrary formal_proof string with empty claims/premises to the shown example.
findings.impact: The documented routine accepts an unverified proof and labels it ready for attestation. Targeted consumer search found only this documentation definition; this is not a demonstrated production authorization bypass.

findings.title: Folder prefix example uses an unbounded lexical lower bound
findings.evidence: The documented starts-with filter contains only operator gte, value docs/api/, with no upper bound or separate prefix predicate.
findings.trigger: Apply the example to a collection also containing lexically later unrelated folders, such as docs/zzz/ or private/.
findings.impact: A greater-than-or-equal comparison does not enforce the claimed prefix and can include unrelated retrieval results. This is a docs/example filter defect, not a demonstrated tenant authorization boundary.

hypotheses.statement: The physical crypto-shredding claim is stronger than DELETE of plaintext rows. No blob encryption/key destruction or WAL/free-page erasure is visible here; assess database/WAL retention before treating this as physical erasure.
hypotheses.reason: No forensic runtime or filesystem byte analysis authorized.
